text: Why are GPUs the default hardware for training large neural networks, even though they were built for graphics?
options: Because they accelerate the linear algebra involved
Because they have fast serial integer arithmetic
Because they use very little power per computation
Because they have large caches for text corpora
answer: Because they accelerate the linear algebra involved
explanation: Every layer of a neural network is a matrix multiply, and GPUs are thousands of cores doing the same operation on thousands of elements at once. Drawing triangles turned out to be the same shape of problem, which is one of the luckiest accidents in the history of computing.

text: Which Google chip is an application specific integrated circuit built specifically for neural network workloads?
explanation: Google started using TPUs internally in 2015 and opened them to third parties through its cloud in 2018. TensorFlow, JAX and PyTorch all support them, and the distinction from an NPU is mostly that Google calls its own product a TPU.

text: What does CUDA stand for?
explanation: Nvidia created it in 2004 and released it in 2007, and it is a platform and API rather than a chip. It is also the reason Nvidia is hard to displace, since the software ecosystem built on it is decades deep and a competitor has to beat the hardware and the tooling at once.

text: High Bandwidth Memory stacks DRAM dies vertically. Which three companies first developed the standard?
explanation: It is a 3D stacked SDRAM interface, and the first HBM chip came from SK Hynix in 2013. Training is frequently memory bandwidth bound rather than compute bound, which is why the HBM supply chain became a chokepoint for the whole industry within about two years.

text: Nvidia's Hopper microarchitecture is designed primarily for which workload?
explanation: Hopper is a datacenter part and sits alongside Lovelace, which is the consumer line. The name comes from Grace Hopper, the naval rear admiral, and the H100 built on it is the chip most of the 2023 to 2025 training runs were done on.

text: Nvidia's Ampere GPU microarchitecture is named after which person?
explanation: The French physicist and mathematician after whom the ampere is named, and Nvidia announced Ampere in May 2020. Nvidia does this consistently, since Blackwell, Hopper and Ampere are all people, and the convention is one of the easier ways to place a card in a timeline.

text: Which company builds the wafer scale engine, a processor built by linking many dies across a single silicon wafer?
explanation: Cerebras in Sunnyvale, California builds a processor the size of a wafer and the CS-3 supercomputers around it, and sells access by API as well. The bet is that model parallelism beats the difficulty of getting a single enormous chip manufactured reliably.

text: An NPU, also called an AI accelerator, is best described as what?
options: A general purpose CPU with a wider instruction set
A type of DRAM stacked in three dimensions
A compiler that targets GPUs instead of CPUs
A specialised hardware accelerator for AI workloads
answer: A specialised hardware accelerator for AI workloads
explanation: It can be standalone, part of a CPU or part of a GPU, and the term is a category rather than a product. The whole category grew out of the observation that neural network inference does a small number of operations very many times, which is a different shape of problem from general purpose computing.

text: Moore's law says the number of transistors on an integrated circuit does what over time?
options: Doubles roughly every two years at near constant cost
Halves roughly every five years at rising cost
Triples every decade at falling cost
Doubles every decade at constant cost
answer: Doubles roughly every two years at near constant cost
explanation: Moore published it as an observation in 1965, not a law, and it described an empirical relationship rather than a physical necessity. It is also the reason people believed AI scaling would be affordable, since compute was on an exponential curve even when the models were not yet good enough to use.

text: Nvidia was founded in 1993 by Jensen Huang and two co-founders. What were the other two names?
explanation: The three founded Nvidia after leaving Sun Microsystems, and the company nearly ran out of money in its first few years. Jensen Huang is the one who stayed famous enough to be the answer to a different question, which is the last question on the founders list.

text: Which foundry manufactures most of Nvidia's AI chips and was founded in 1987 by Morris Chang?
explanation: TSMC pioneered the pure-play foundry model and fabs Nvidia's datacenter GPUs, including Blackwell on its 4NP process. Samsung is the tempting miss because it also fabs advanced chips, but Nvidia's AI lineup runs overwhelmingly through TSMC.

text: Which company is the sole supplier of extreme ultraviolet lithography machines for advanced chips?
explanation: The Dutch firm ASML holds a near-monopoly on EUV systems printing 5 nm and 3 nm layers at 13.5 nm wavelength. Nikon is the tempting miss because it once led lithography with Canon, but neither ships EUV machines today.

text: Nvidia's Blackwell architecture is named after which person?
explanation: David Blackwell was the statistician behind game theory and probability work that underpins modern ML, honored at GTC 2024 with the B200 datacenter accelerators. Grace Hopper is the tempting miss because Hopper is the preceding Nvidia architecture, also named for a person.

text: Which Nvidia chip became the workhorse of AI training during the 2022 to 2024 boom?
explanation: The Hopper-based H100 powered most frontier training runs of the boom, succeeding the Ampere A100. The A100 is the tempting miss because it was the previous workhorse, but by 2023 waitlists and headlines all pointed at H100 supply.

text: How many GPUs did Nvidia's DGX-1 contain, the system whose first unit was delivered to OpenAI in 2016?
explanation: The DGX-1 packed 8 Pascal P100 GPUs linked by NVLink, and Jensen Huang hand-delivered the first box to OpenAI. Sixteen is the tempting miss because later DGX generations scaled up, but the original 2016 box held eight.

text: What does the LPU in Groq's chip name stand for?
explanation: Groq rebranded its tensor streaming chip as the Language Processing Unit for LLM inference, and its 2024 speed demos went viral. Linear Processing Unit is the tempting miss because it sounds like standard hardware jargon, but the official expansion is Language, which also fueled confusion with xAI's Grok chatbot.

text: Most advanced AI chips are fabbed in Taiwan. Which of these follows from that concentration?
options: A disruption there would affect only consumer devices
A disruption there could trigger a worldwide chip shortage
A disruption there would make AI models cheaper to train
A disruption there would remove the need for new chip designs
answer: A disruption there could trigger a worldwide chip shortage
explanation: One company on one island makes the dies for the accelerators every AI lab rents, and a fabrication plant takes years to build, so the capacity cannot be replaced quickly if it stops. That dependency is expensive for everyone else to escape, which is the idea behind Taiwan's silicon shield. TSMC is spreading capacity to Arizona partly to soften exactly this risk.
answerAliases: a disruption could cause another worldwide chip shortage
commanding majority in the semiconductor foundry market

text: ASML makes the only machines in the world that can print the smallest features on a chip. Which of these follows?
options: Chipmakers can make the same nodes with older machines
Chipmakers no longer need to buy lithography equipment
Chipmakers can copy the machines once patents expire
Chipmakers at the smallest nodes buy from one supplier
answer: Chipmakers at the smallest nodes buy from one supplier
explanation: EUV is the only way to print the layers at 5 nm and 3 nm, so every advanced chipmaker queues for the same supplier. The dependency is concrete: Intel put $4.1 billion into ASML in 2012 for a 15 percent stake, and Samsung and TSMC took smaller stakes under the same program, so the customers helped pay for the tool they all need. Nikon and Canon once led lithography, but neither ships EUV machines.
answerAliases: the world's only manufacturer of extreme ultraviolet (EUV) lithography machines
required to manufacture the most advanced semiconductor chips
largest supplier to the semiconductor industry

text: Phone chips from Apple, Qualcomm and Samsung now carry a dedicated neural network accelerator. What is it mainly for?
options: Running small AI models efficiently on low power
Training large language models from scratch on the phone
Replacing the graphics chip used to render phone games
Compressing photos and video to save phone storage
answer: Running small AI models efficiently on low power
explanation: On a phone the accelerator is deliberately small and power-efficient, sized to run little models rather than train them, and a phone running a large model on its main cores would be hot and flat within minutes. Keeping the work on the device also means the data never has to leave the phone. Data centre accelerators make the opposite bet: far bigger, and happy to be noisy.

text: Nvidia paid $6.9 billion for Mellanox, closing the deal in 2020. What did it get that mattered for AI clusters?
options: A chip foundry that could manufacture its own silicon
A competing AI accelerator it could rebrand and retire
InfiniBand networking for linking huge GPU clusters
A controlling stake in the ARM instruction set
answer: InfiniBand networking for linking huge GPU clusters
explanation: Mellanox built InfiniBand adapters and switches, the fabric that stitches thousands of GPUs into a single training job instead of leaving them a room of separate boxes. InfiniBand competes with Ethernet for that job, and having both under one roof is why a cluster is now sold as a system rather than as chips. The company was folded into Nvidia's networking division, and the Mellanox name disappeared from new products.
answerAliases: based on InfiniBand and Ethernet technology

text: Groq and Grok are two different AI things that get mixed up constantly. Which pairing is right?
options: Grok is the chip company, Groq is the chatbot
Groq is the chip company, Grok is the chatbot
Groq is the chatbot, Grok is the chip company
Both are the same company, spelled two ways
answer: Groq is the chip company, Grok is the chatbot
explanation: Groq builds the inference accelerator it calls the LPU, originally a Tensor Streaming Processor, and its speed demos went viral. Grok is the chatbot and model family from SpaceXAI, named after the verb in Heinlein's Stranger in a Strange Land. The one-letter gap between the two names is why they get crossed so often.
answerAliases: builds an AI accelerator application-specific integrated circuit
American artificial intelligence (AI) company that builds

text: An AI accelerator's HBM sits on the same package as the GPU and is joined to it over a link more than a thousand bits wide. What does that width buy?
options: Little, since AI chips are limited by compute rather than bandwidth
A wide path, so weights reach the GPU's arithmetic units faster
Enough capacity to hold a whole model's weights on one card
A cheaper way to build memory than ordinary DDR modules
answer: A wide path, so weights reach the GPU's arithmetic units faster
explanation: A single HBM stack presents a 1024-bit bus to the chip sitting next to it, where a single graphics memory channel is 32 bits, and the dies in the stack are wired together through silicon vias. The point is supply rate rather than storage: a GPU full of arithmetic units sits idle if the weights arrive slowly. Capacity is a separate figure and more layers do raise it, but that is not why the bus is so wide.
answerAliases: The HBM memory bus is very wide in comparison to other DRAM memories such as DDR4 or GDDR5
higher bandwidth than DDR4 or GDDR5
a width of 1024 bits in total

text: HBM, the memory stacked onto AI accelerators, comes from a very small group of suppliers. Which of these four companies is one of them?
explanation: Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron make almost all of the world's HBM, which is why the same three names turn up on every accelerator data sheet. The other names here are storage companies rather than HBM suppliers: Kioxia and Western Digital live in flash, and Nanya makes conventional server DRAM without an HBM line. HBM earns more per wafer than DDR5, so the AI boom has squeezed ordinary DRAM supply as a side effect.
answerAliases: SK Hynix, Samsung Electronics, and Micron Technology

text: The 'double' in the name DDR5 memory refers to what?
options: Data moving on both edges of the clock signal
The number of memory banks inside each chip
The number of bits stored in each memory cell
The rate at which a module refreshes its stored data
answer: Data moving on both edges of the clock signal
explanation: DDR stands for double data rate: the memory moves data on the rising and falling edges of the clock, so a 100 MHz bus is sold as 1600 MT/s. That is why an advertised module speed is twice the physical clock, and the doubling has nothing to do with cells or banks. DDR5 also happens to have two 32-bit subchannels per module, a separate change that confuses anyone reading a spec sheet.
answerAliases: transferring data on both the rising and falling edges of the clock signal
both the rising and falling clock edges

text: A rack full of AI accelerators pumps coolant through cold plates bolted to the chips instead of just blowing room air over them. How does the heat leave the chip?
options: Chilled air pumped up from under the data centre floor blown across the die
Liquid metal filling the plate soaks up the heat like a sponge and holds it
Coolant flowing through the plate absorbs the heat and carries it away
The coolant boiling on contact and its vapour lifting the heat off the die
answer: Coolant flowing through the plate absorbs the heat and carries it away
explanation: A pump pushes coolant through a water block bonded to the chip and out to a heat exchanger, which is the same loop a water cooled car engine runs. Water shifts heat far better than air, and AI racks need it because a full rack of accelerators has gone past what fans can move: immersion designs are rated near 100 kW per 19-inch rack where air cooling stops around 23 kW. Liquid metal fills the gap between chip and plate, and boiling coolant belongs to two phase immersion, neither of which is the cold plate loop.
answerAliases: the water being circulated by a water pump through a water block mounted on the CPU
out to a heat exchanger, typically a radiator
Direct Liquid Cooling (DLC) with cold plates for cooling chips in servers

text: Data centre operators quote a figure called PUE when they talk about how efficiently a building runs. What does that number measure?
options: The share of a data centre's power spent on cooling instead of computing
How efficiently the servers themselves turn electricity into useful work
How much power a data centre draws per terabyte of data it stores
A facility's total power draw divided by the power its computing gear uses
answer: A facility's total power draw divided by the power its computing gear uses
explanation: PUE is total facility energy divided by the energy that actually reaches computing equipment, and a perfect building would score 1.0. Anything that is not a server, an accelerator or a network switch counts as overhead, cooling and lighting included, so a PUE of 1.2 means twenty percent extra energy burned on everything else. It says nothing about how well the chips themselves turn power into useful work, which is the gap researchers were complaining about when they proposed compute-centric metrics instead.
answerAliases: PUE is the ratio of the total amount of energy used by a computer data center facility to the energy delivered to computing equipment

text: A chip designer draws up the blueprints and leaves the making to someone else. What is a chip foundry there to do?
options: A company that designs chips and licenses them to be built
A factory that makes chips from other companies' designs
A plant that buys finished chips and resells them under its own label
A company that assembles finished chips into laptops and servers
answer: A factory that makes chips from other companies' designs
explanation: A foundry is the factory: it owns the clean room and the process, and turns somebody else's design into silicon, which is why it is also called a fab. Pure-play means it does not draw up chip designs of its own, so TSMC can build chips for Nvidia and AMD without competing with them. The older arrangement was the integrated device manufacturer, which designed and fabbed under one roof, and the rise of fabless companies like Nvidia is what split those two jobs apart.
answerAliases: also called a fab or a foundry, is a factory where integrated circuits (ICs) are manufactured

text: Extreme ultraviolet lithography is the process behind the smallest features on modern chips. What does the machine actually do to a wafer?
options: Shoots ions into the wafer to change how it conducts
Etches material between layers to cut the vertical features
Cuts each finished chip out of the wafer surface
Projects a circuit pattern onto a light sensitive coating
answer: Projects a circuit pattern onto a light sensitive coating
explanation: EUV is a light source: it projects a circuit pattern onto a light sensitive coating called photoresist, and later steps copy that pattern down into the silicon. The light sits at 13.5 nm, a band ordinary lenses cannot carry at all, so the optics bounce it off mirrors instead of refracting it through glass. Ion implantation and etching are genuine steps in the same factory and dicing happens at the very end, but none of them is lithography.
answerAliases: create intricate patterns on semiconductor substrates
to produce a pattern by using a reflective photomask to expose a substrate covered by photoresist

text: The smallest process nodes, the ones AI accelerators are built on, come out of foundries run by the same three companies. Which three?
explanation: TSMC, Samsung and Intel are the three that operate foundries at the smallest nodes, and every recent generation from 7 nm down has been built by those same names. GlobalFoundries, UMC and Tower are real foundries that deliberately stopped short of the newest nodes, because a plant for them costs billions and their customers do not need them. Intel is also the company that quietly dropped the nanometer suffix from its node names, calling its newest process 18A instead.

text: A chipmaker advertises a chip built on a 3 nm process. What does that label actually tell you?
options: A physical size, with the smallest feature at 3 nm
The area the finished chip covers on the die
The generation of process it belongs to, not a size
The switching speed of one transistor, in nanoseconds
answer: The generation of process it belongs to, not a size
explanation: Nothing on the chip measures 3 nm any more: the name has been a generation label rather than a physical size for years, and the figure matches no gate length or metal pitch at all. What it does reliably mean is more transistors packed into the same area, built with more machines and more process steps. The sharpest reminder is that TSMC and Samsung shipped the same 3 nm label on very different transistors, FinFETs for one and gate-all-around for the other.
answerAliases: no direct relation to any actual physical feature
used primarily as a marketing term
new, improved generation of silicon semiconductor chips

text: TSMC sells CoWoS as advanced packaging for AI accelerators. What does it do?
options: Prints the transistor layers at a tighter node than a fab
Tests every die and discards the ones that fail
Cuts a finished wafer into separate chips for shipping
Merges several dies into one package as a single device
answer: Merges several dies into one package as a single device
explanation: Advanced packaging puts two or more dies into one package and wires them together so that the pair behaves like a single chip, and CoWoS does it over an interposer that carries the connections. It exists because shrinking one monolithic die keeps getting harder, so the industry bought performance back by connecting dies instead of drawing more of them. Dicing the wafer and sorting the good dies are real steps too, but they bracket this one rather than being it.

source.title: Advanced packaging (semiconductors)
source.label: Advanced packaging in semiconductors on Wikipedia

answerAliases: TSMC's CoWoS (chip-on-wafer-on-substrate) technology, which uses an interposer
to be merged and packaged as a single electronic device
combining logic (processors) and memory in a single package

text: What are tensor cores in Nvidia GPUs specially designed to speed up?
options: The encryption of data at rest
explanation: Tensor cores are units that multiply small matrices and are intended to speed up the training of neural networks, which is why every datacenter Nvidia GPU since Volta has carried them. Rendering, video encoding and encryption are real GPU workloads, but they run on the CUDA cores, the RT and NVENC engines, or the host, not on tensor cores.

text: Which Nvidia microarchitecture was the first to feature tensor cores?
explanation: Volta, announced in May 2017 and first shipped in the Tesla V100, was Nvidia's first chip to feature tensor cores. Pascal is the tempting miss because it powered the DGX-1 that Jensen Huang hand-delivered to OpenAI in 2016, but it had no tensor cores.

text: Which Nvidia microarchitecture introduced dedicated ray tracing cores, or RT cores?
explanation: Turing, introduced in August 2018, was the first architecture with dedicated RT cores for real-time ray tracing, alongside second-generation tensor cores. Ampere is the tempting miss because it refined ray tracing performance, but the dedicated hardware arrived with Turing.

text: Which A100 feature lets a single GPU be split into up to seven independent instances?
explanation: MIG partitions one A100 into up to seven separate instances, each with its own memory and compute, so a cloud can sell fractional GPUs without one tenant seeing another. NVLink 3.0 is the GPU-to-GPU interconnect, and TF32 and sparsity are tensor core features, none of which split the card.

text: Nvidia created NVLink to beat the bandwidth limits of which older interconnect?
explanation: NVLink was built because PCI Express could not move data fast enough between CPUs and GPUs or between GPUs themselves; the first NVLink offered 20 GB/s per link against PCIe 3.0's 8 GT/s per lane. USB, SATA and Thunderbolt are peripheral buses that never carried GPU traffic at all.

text: Which company launched the MI300 series as its flagship generative AI accelerator?
explanation: AMD announced the MI300A and MI300X in 2023 as its answer to Nvidia's H100, building them on the CDNA 3 architecture with chiplets and HBM3. Intel sells the Gaudi line, and Qualcomm and Samsung have not shipped a datacenter GPU of this class.

text: Which Apple chip was the first to include a Neural Engine?
explanation: The A11 Bionic, shipped in the iPhone 8 and iPhone X in 2017, was Apple's first chip with a Neural Engine, rated at 600 billion operations per second for Face ID and Animoji. The M1 is the tempting miss because it is Apple's most famous AI chip, but the Neural Engine debuted four years earlier in the A11.

text: Google's first-generation TPU, shipped in 2016, was built mainly for which kind of workload?
explanation: The first TPU was an 8-bit matrix multiplication engine for inference, running search ranking, photo processing and Street View text recognition, and Google was still using CPUs and GPUs for training. The second-generation TPU in 2017 was the first Google chip built for both training and inference.

text: Which generation of Google's TPU added training support alongside inference?
explanation: The second-generation TPU, announced in May 2017, added floating point and the bfloat16 format, which made it useful for both training and inference, and Google called it the industry's first production deep-learning training chip. The first generation was integer-only and inference-bound, and the later generations refined performance rather than adding the training capability.

text: Which British semiconductor company builds the Intelligence Processing Unit, or IPU?
explanation: Graphcore, founded in Bristol in 2016 by Simon Knowles and Nigel Toon, introduced the massively parallel Intelligence Processing Unit that holds the whole model on-chip. Cerebras builds a wafer-scale chip, Groq builds the LPU, and SambaNova builds the RDU, none of which is called an IPU.

text: Why did Nvidia create the H800 and A800 variants of its Hopper GPUs in 2022?
options: To replace the H100 with a faster part
To comply with US export restrictions on chips to China
To enter the gaming GPU market
To switch to a cheaper Samsung process
answer: To comply with US export restrictions on chips to China
explanation: In late 2022, US regulations limited exports of advanced chips to China, so Nvidia adapted the H100 into the H800 with lower interconnect bandwidth, and the A800 was the Ampere equivalent; both were later swept up in new US restrictions in 2023. They were cut-down parts, not faster or cheaper ones, and Nvidia's gaming line was never the point.

text: What was the main goal of the 2022 CHIPS and Science Act?
options: To ban AI exports to China
To fund semiconductor manufacturing subsidies in the United States
To create a national social media company
answer: To fund semiconductor manufacturing subsidies in the United States
explanation: Signed by President Biden in August 2022, the act appropriated $52.7 billion, including $39 billion in subsidies for chip manufacturing on US soil, to reduce dependence on overseas fabs. It was about building plants at home, not about export bans, social media or space.

source.title: CHIPS and Science Act
source.label: CHIPS and Science Act on Wikipedia

text: In 2024 Amazon agreed to buy a 960-megawatt nuclear-powered data center campus from which company?
explanation: Amazon bought the data center campus next to Talen's Susquehanna nuclear plant in Pennsylvania for $650 million, with a power purchase agreement for up to 1,920 MW through 2042. Constellation is the tempting miss because it is the company restarting Three Mile Island for Microsoft, but the Susquehanna deal belongs to Talen.

source.label: Talen Energy press release via SEC EDGAR

text: Jim Keller was the lead architect of which AMD microarchitecture?
explanation: Keller led the AMD K8 microarchitecture, which became the original Athlon 64 and introduced the x86-64 instruction set. Zen is the tempting miss because Keller returned to AMD in 2012 to work on Zen's early design, but the K8 was his defining AMD work.

text: Jim Keller became CEO of which AI chip startup in 2023?
explanation: Keller joined Tenstorrent as CTO in 2020 and became CEO in January 2023, leading the company that builds AI chips based on RISC-V. Cerebras, d-Matrix and Etched are real AI chip startups, but none of them is run by Keller.

text: Who became Intel's CEO in February 2021?
explanation: Gelsinger rejoined Intel as CEO on February 15, 2021, after 30 years at the company including a stint as CTO. Lip-Bu Tan is the tempting miss because he later succeeded Gelsinger as Intel's CEO, but he took over in 2025, not 2021.

text: Before co-founding Nvidia, Jensen Huang worked at AMD and which other company?
explanation: Huang left AMD for LSI Logic and then worked with Sun Microsystems, where he met Chris Malachowsky and Curtis Priem; the three founded Nvidia together in 1993. Texas Instruments and Intel were places he was recruited to, but he chose AMD first, and Sun is where the Nvidia founding team met.

text: Which company abandoned its attempted $40 billion acquisition of Arm in February 2022?
explanation: Nvidia announced the Arm acquisition in September 2020 for $40 billion in stock and cash, but regulators in the UK, EU and US raised competition and national security concerns, and the deal collapsed in February 2022. Microsoft, AMD and Intel were all reported as interested parties at various points, but only Nvidia signed and then abandoned the deal.

text: Nvidia's Grace datacenter CPU is named after which computer scientist?
explanation: Nvidia has said it named both its 2024 CPU generation Grace and its GPU generation Hopper after Grace Hopper, the Navy rear admiral and COBOL pioneer. Ada Lovelace is the tempting miss because Nvidia's consumer architecture also bears her name, but the datacenter CPU honors Hopper.

text: What is the name of Nvidia's module that combines a Grace CPU with a Hopper GPU?
explanation: The GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip pairs a Hopper-based H100 GPU with a Grace-based 72-core CPU on a single module, connected by NVLink for memory coherence. GB200 is the Blackwell successor, and DGX-1 and HGX H100 are systems rather than the CPU-GPU module.

text: Which GPU cloud company was created in 2024 from the restructuring of Yandex?
explanation: Yandex N.V. sold its Russian assets in July 2024 and renamed itself Nebius Group, keeping the cloud and AI infrastructure business with CEO Arkady Volozh. CoreWeave, Lambda and Crusoe are all real neoclouds, but none of them came out of Yandex.

text: How many INT8 operations per clock can one Nvidia tensor core perform?
explanation: Each tensor core does 128 INT8 operations per clock, twice the 64 FP16 operations, because one FP16 multiply-accumulate maps to two INT8 ones at the same width. The 1024 figure is the INT1 rate and 256 is INT4, which is why INT8 is the sweet spot for inference speed on the same silicon.

source.title: Deep Learning Super Sampling
source.label: Deep Learning Super Sampling on Wikipedia

text: Nvidia's platform of edge AI computers for robotics is called?
explanation: Jetson is Nvidia's family of compact edge AI modules, from the Nano to the Thor, built for robots and on-device inference. Drive is the automotive platform, BlueField is the networking DPU, and EGX is the enterprise edge server line, none of which is the robotics module brand.

text: Which Stanford spinout builds the Reconfigurable Dataflow Unit, or RDU?
explanation: SambaNova, founded by Kunle Olukotun and others from Stanford, builds the RDU, a dataflow processor designed so models are compiled into the hardware's reconfigurable fabric. Graphcore builds the IPU, Groq builds the LPU, and Cerebras builds a wafer-scale engine, none of which is the RDU.

text: Tesla designed which custom supercomputer around its D1 chip to train Full Self-Driving networks?
explanation: Dojo, announced at Tesla's AI Day in August 2021, is built from D1 chips on training tiles and went into production in 2023. The FSD Computer and HW3 are the inference chips in customer cars, and the Autopilot cluster is the older Nvidia A100-based training fleet, not the custom D1 machine.

text: Which H100 form factor is the standard for training clusters?
explanation: The H100 SXM5 is the socketed module used in DGX and HGX systems, and Nvidia says it offers better performance than the PCIe variant because of the higher power budget and NVLink bandwidth. PCIe is the tempting miss because it is the familiar plug-in card format, but training clusters run SXM5.

text: What does an NVSwitch add to an NVLink system?
options: A central switch connecting many GPUs
A faster clock for each GPU
answer: A central switch connecting many GPUs
explanation: A few GPUs can mesh directly over NVLink, but beyond that a central NVSwitch serves up to 32 ports so every GPU can talk to every other at full bandwidth. It does not change clocks, add memory or carry power, which is why the switch is about connectivity, not compute.

text: The DGX H100 and DGX GH200 systems include which Nvidia data processing unit?
explanation: DGX systems ship with BlueField-3 DPUs to offload networking, storage and security from the CPUs and GPUs. ConnectX-7 is the InfiniBand NIC, Quantum-2 is the InfiniBand switch, and Spectrum-X is the Ethernet platform, none of which is the DPU.

text: Which Nvidia datacenter GPU was the first to support HBM3?
explanation: The Hopper H100 supports HBM3 and HBM2e, raising memory bandwidth 50 percent over the A100's HBM2. The A100 is the tempting miss because it was the previous workhorse, but it shipped with HBM2, and the V100 before it used HBM2 as well.

text: Which TSMC node was the first commercially available extreme ultraviolet lithography process?
explanation: TSMC's N7+ was the first commercially available EUV process, used in 2020, before N5, N3 and N2 added more EUV layers. N5 is the tempting miss because it is the most famous EUV node, but N7+ was the first to bring EUV into high-volume production.

text: How much HBM memory does the H100 support?
explanation: The H100 ships with up to 80 GB of HBM3 across five stacks, delivering 3.35 TB/s of bandwidth. The 192 GB figure belongs to the later B200, and 141 GB is the H200, so the H100's 80 GB is the number to remember for the 2022 generation.

text: What is the name of Nvidia's 72-GPU Blackwell rack-scale system announced at GTC 2024?
explanation: The GB200 NVL72 connects 36 Grace CPUs and 72 B200 GPUs in one liquid-cooled rack that acts as a single giant GPU. HGX B200 is the 8-GPU board, DGX SuperPOD is the multi-rack system, and DGX GB200 is the server, none of which is the 72-GPU rack.

text: Nvidia's Rubin microarchitecture, announced in 2024, is named after which astrophysicist?
explanation: Rubin is named after the astrophysicist Vera Rubin, whose dark matter work made her one of the most famous astronomers of the 20th century. Grace Hopper and Ada Lovelace are the tempting misses because Nvidia names architectures after pioneers, but the preceding Blackwell was named for David Blackwell and Rubin is the next generation.

source.label: NVIDIA Newsroom on the Rubin platform (named for Vera Rubin)

text: The MI300 series accelerators are built on which AMD architecture?
explanation: The MI300A and MI300X use the CDNA 3 architecture, AMD's datacenter GPU lineage with chiplets and HBM3. RDNA 3 is the consumer Radeon architecture, and GCN 5 is the older Instinct line, so CDNA 3 is the correct family for the MI300.

text: How much HBM3 memory does the MI300X carry?
explanation: The MI300X packs 192 GB of HBM3 with 5.3 TB/s of bandwidth, which was the largest memory footprint of any GPU at launch in 2023. The 288 GB figure belongs to the later MI350X, and 128 GB is the MI300A's smaller allocation.

text: AMD's Zen 2 moved to which physical design that separated core dies from the I/O die?
explanation: Zen 2 combined up to eight 7 nm core chiplets with a single 14 nm I/O die, letting AMD put the expensive cores on the small node and the I/O on a mature one. A monolithic die puts everything on one piece, wafer stacking bonds whole wafers, and system-in-package is a broader term, but the design that defined Zen 2 was the chiplet.

text: How many cores per socket did the Epyc Rome server processors carry?
explanation: Epyc Rome, launched in August 2019 on Zen 2, doubled the core count per socket to 64 cores with 128 threads. The 32 cores figure belongs to the first-generation Naples, and 96 cores is the later Genoa, so 64 is the Rome number.

text: In 2021 Intel renamed its 10 nm Enhanced SuperFin process to what?
explanation: At its July 2021 Intel Accelerated event, Intel introduced a new naming structure and rebranded 10 nm SuperFin as Intel 7, aligning its names with how TSMC and Samsung label nodes. Intel 4, Intel 3 and Intel 18A are all later nodes in the same roadmap, not the renamed 10 nm process.

source.label: Intel Accelerates Process and Packaging Innovations press release

text: When did Pat Gelsinger step down as Intel's CEO?
explanation: Gelsinger stepped down on December 1, 2024, after 3 years and 10 months as CEO, with David Zinsser and Michelle Johnston Holthaus named interim co-CEOs. Intel's troubles continued after his departure, which is why the 2024 date, not 2025, is the one to remember.

text: How many transistors does the Nvidia H100 contain?
explanation: The H100 is built on TSMC's N4 process with 80 billion transistors. The 208 billion figure belongs to the B200's dual-die package, 104 billion is the GB100 die, and 54 billion is the A100, so 80 billion is the H100's count.

text: How many transistors does the Nvidia B200 package contain?
explanation: The B200 combines two GB100 dies of 104 billion transistors each in a single package for a total of 208 billion, connected by a 10 TB/s link called NV-HBI. The 104 billion figure is one die, which is the tempting miss, but the package total is 208 billion.

text: Which numeric format, introduced with Ampere's tensor cores, gives FP32 range at tensor core speed?
explanation: TensorFloat-32, or TF32, keeps the 8-bit exponent of FP32 but shortens the mantissa, letting tensor cores handle training math with FP32's dynamic range. BF16 is the tempting miss because it is also a training format, but it was introduced on Google's TPU, not with Ampere, and FP8 and INT4 came later.

text: Which CPU cores does AMD's MI300A integrate alongside its GPU chiplets?
explanation: The MI300A is an APU that pairs 24 Zen 4 CPU cores with four CDNA 3 GPU chiplets and 128 GB of HBM3. Zen 2 and Zen 3 are the tempting misses because they powered the earlier Epyc generations, but the MI300A moved to Zen 4 on the 5 nm node.

text: Which Apple chip was the first widely available SoC built on a 3 nm process?
explanation: The A17 Pro, in the iPhone 15 Pro and iPad Mini 7 in 2023, was the first widely available 3 nm SoC, fabbed by TSMC on its N3 process with 19 billion transistors. The A15 and A16 are the tempting misses because they are the immediately preceding chips, but both were built on 5 nm, and the M1 was 5 nm as well.

text: Which Nvidia architecture was the first to implement the Transformer Engine?
explanation: Hopper's Transformer Engine dynamically lowers precision from FP16 to FP8 during inference when the accuracy loss is acceptable, which is why the H100 became the transformer training chip. Ampere is the tempting miss because it introduced TF32 and sparsity, but the Transformer Engine itself arrived with Hopper.

text: Nvidia's Grace datacenter CPU is based on which instruction set architecture?
explanation: Grace is built on ARM's Neoverse V2 cores, which is why the GH200 pairs it with Hopper over NVLink for memory coherence. x86-64 is the tempting miss because Nvidia's DGX systems had long used Intel and AMD CPUs, but Grace marked Nvidia's move to ARM.

text: The GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip module has a total power draw of up to?
explanation: The GH200 module, with a Grace CPU and an H100 GPU, can draw up to 1000 W. The 700 W figure is the H100 SXM5 GPU alone, which is the tempting miss, but the full CPU-GPU module pushes past it.

text: Which Amazon Web Services chip line is custom-built for AI training?
explanation: AWS's Annapurna Labs builds the Trainium line of AI training ASICs, with Trainium2 powering large training jobs for Anthropic's Claude. Inferentia is the inference counterpart, Graviton is the general-purpose CPU, and Nitro handles networking and storage offload, so Trainium is the training answer.

text: Google's purpose-built edge AI chip, announced in 2018, is called?
explanation: The Edge TPU, announced in July 2018, is Google's ASIC for running ML models on-device in the Coral products, at 4 trillion operations per second on 2 watts. The Pixel Neural Core is the Edge TPU's name inside the Pixel 4 phone, Tensor G2 is the phone SoC, and Coral is the product brand, not the chip.

text: Which company launched the Gaudi 3 AI accelerator in April 2024?
explanation: Intel launched Gaudi 3 at its Intel Vision event in April 2024, building on the Gaudi 2 it inherited with the Habana Labs acquisition. AMD's answer is the MI300, Nvidia's is the H100, and Qualcomm's is the Cloud AI 100, so Gaudi 3 belongs to Intel.

text: Which AI startup did Intel acquire in 2016 for about $408 million?
explanation: Intel acquired Nervana Systems on August 9, 2016, for an estimated $408 million, and later shut down its chip development in 2020 in favor of Habana Labs. Movidius is the tempting miss because Intel also bought it in 2016, but for computer vision chips, and Altera was a much larger $16.7 billion deal in 2015.

text: Intel's Neural Compute Stick was built around chips from which 2016 acquisition?
explanation: The Intel Movidius Neural Compute Stick used the Myriad 2 vision processing unit that Intel acquired with Movidius in September 2016, and the NCS 2 used the Myriad X. Nervana was a software and datacenter AI startup, Altera made FPGAs, and Mobileye makes autonomous driving chips, none of which powered the stick.

text: IBM's 2014 neuromorphic chip with just over a million simulated neurons is called?
explanation: TrueNorth, produced by IBM in 2014, packed 4096 cores with just over a million neurons and 268 million synapses on a 70 mW chip. NorthPole is the tempting miss because it is IBM's 2023 follow-up, but the million-neuron 2014 chip was TrueNorth, and SyNAPSE was the research program name.

text: Which AWS chip offloads networking and storage from the main server?
explanation: AWS Nitro is the hardware that handles networking, storage and security offload in every AWS server since 2015, letting the main CPUs run customer workloads. Graviton is the CPU, Trainium is the training ASIC, and Inferentia is the inference ASIC, so Nitro is the offload answer.

text: Which company shipped the first 3 nm gate-all-around process in 2022?
explanation: Samsung started shipping its 3 nm gate-all-around process, called 3GAA, in mid-2022, beating TSMC's 3 nm to market with a different transistor structure. TSMC is the tempting miss because it dominates advanced nodes, but its 3 nm kept FinFET and arrived later that year.

text: Nvidia's GB100 Blackwell die sits at what manufacturing limit?
explanation: The GB100 die is at the reticle limit, the maximum area a lithography machine can expose in one shot, which is why Nvidia pairs two dies in one package instead of making a bigger one. Thermal, yield and wafer limits are real constraints, but the single-die ceiling that shaped Blackwell is the reticle limit.

text: Qualcomm's first custom digital signal processor in Snapdragon was called?
explanation: The Snapdragon SoC, announced in 2006, included Qualcomm's first custom Hexagon DSP. Adreno is the GPU, Kryo is the CPU core, and Spectra is the image signal processor, so Hexagon is the DSP that has carried Snapdragon's signal processing for two decades.

text: Which transistor architecture does Intel's 18A process node introduce?
explanation: Intel 18A combines RibbonFET, Intel's gate-all-around transistor, with PowerVia backside power delivery, and the first products powered on in 2024. FinFET is the tempting miss because it powered Intel's previous nodes, but 18A is the first Intel node with the new transistor architecture.

source.label: Intel Foundry Achieves Major Milestones press release

text: Which Nvidia consumer GPU family was fabbed on Samsung's custom 8 nm process?
explanation: Ampere's consumer GeForce RTX 30 series used a custom Samsung 8 nm process called 8N, while the datacenter A100 was fabbed on TSMC's 7 nm. The RTX 40 series is the tempting miss because it is the next consumer generation, but it moved to TSMC's 4 nm.

text: The SpiNNaker neuromorphic supercomputer architecture was designed at which university?
explanation: SpiNNaker was designed by the Advanced Processor Technologies Research Group at the University of Manchester, as a manycore machine for simulating spiking neural networks. ETH, Cambridge and Munich all have neuromorphic research groups, but the SpiNNaker architecture itself is Manchester's.
